default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1188.title: Autocorrelation regime switch
E-1188.hypothesis: When the rolling lag-1 return autocorrelation is strongly negative, bars are bid-ask bounce and a large bar is faded; when strongly positive, orders are being sliced into the market and a large bar is followed.

E-1189.title: Same-clock forward drift
E-1189.hypothesis: Some clock windows (macro releases, NY open, fund rebalancing) drift the same way in most recent sessions; trade in the direction of the average forward move that followed this minute in the last 20 sessions.

E-1190.title: Volume absorption after a move
E-1190.hypothesis: A high-volume bar with a tiny range after a run means passive limit orders absorbed the aggressors; the run is exhausted so fade it.

E-1191.title: Fast/slow range expansion start
E-1191.hypothesis: When the short-term average bar range jumps above the one-hour average, a volatility regime begins and the move that triggered it tends to continue as stops and momentum orders arrive.

E-1192.title: Session-volume-climax extreme fade
E-1192.hypothesis: The highest-volume bar of the session printing at a fresh local extreme is capitulation or blow-off; late participants are trapped, so fade the extreme.

E-1193.title: Wick-imbalance accumulation
E-1193.hypothesis: Several recent bars with long lower wicks and short upper wicks show repeated rejection of lower prices by patient buyers; buy (and the mirror for sellers) when the rolling wick imbalance gets large.

E-1194.title: Momentum acceleration
E-1194.hypothesis: A move that is not only large but at least twice as fast as the preceding equal window shows urgency (forced flow), which continues for a few more bars.

E-1195.title: Lunch-box breakout
E-1195.hypothesis: The thin lunch period builds a box; the first close beyond it after 13:00 comes with returning liquidity and positioning for the afternoon, so follow it.

E-1196.title: Persistent new-extreme making
E-1196.hypothesis: When many of the recent bars each set a new session high with no new low, buyers are lifting every offer in sequence; the persistent pressure carries on.

E-1197.title: Aged-extreme stop run (Turtle Soup)
E-1197.hypothesis: A swing extreme untouched for several bars collects resting stops beyond it; a poke through it that closes back inside is a stop run with no follow-through, so fade it.
